body.p: In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 18-20, and 25-31. By the present response, the Applicant amends claims 18-20, and 25-31, and adds new claims 32-35. The amendments and new claims do not add any new matter, and support can be found in at least paragraphs 35-42, 44, 46-49, 56, and 57 of the originally filed application. Upon entry of these amendments and new claims, claims 18-20, and 25-35 will be pending in the present application and are believed to be in condition for allowance. In view of the foregoing amendments and the following interview summary and remarks, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of all pending claims.

A telephonic interview with the Examiner and the Applicant's representative, Madison West (Reg. No. 78,838), was conducted on December 23, 2024. During the interview, the partiesdiscussed proposed claim amendments to overcome the rejection of claims 20, 26, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b), the rejection of claims 18-20, 25-29, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 101, and the rejection of independent claim 18 under 35 U.S.C. § 102. With regards to the rejection under 35 U.S.C. §§ 112(b) and 101, the Examiner agreed that the proposed amendments appear to overcome the current rejections. With regards to the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102, the Examiner agreed that the proposed amendments appear to overcome the current rejection though further search and consideration may be required. The amendments to claims 18, 20, 26, and 31 presented herein generally correspond to the proposed amendments that were discussed during the interview. The Applicant welcomes the Examiner to contact the Applicant's representatives with any further suggested amendments to move the application toward allowance. The Applicant thanks the Examiner for their courtesy in granting and conducting the interview.

In the Office Action, the Examiner objected to claim 30 for minor informalities. See Office Action, page 2. The Applicant respectfully submits that claim 30 has been amended to recite, "the usage data comprises a number of occlusion of the tubing system, a duration of use, a number of uses/connections of the tubing system to the C02 sensing system, a number of uses/connections of

the tubing system to an additional CO2 sensing system, or any combination thereof." The Applicant submits that the amendments to claim 30 correct the minor informalities noted by the Examiner. In view of these amendments, the Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the objection to claim 30.

In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 20, 26, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being allegedly indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor regards as the invention. See Office Action, page 2. The Applicant respectfully submits that amended claims 20, 26, and 31 are definite and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention. Indeed, as mentioned in the Interview Summary above, the Examiner indicated that the amendments presented in amended claims 20, 26, and 31 appear to overcome the current rejection. Thus, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of claims 20, 26, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b).

In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 18-20, 25-29, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to an abstract idea of a mental process without significantly more. See Office Action, page 3. The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
Legal Precedent and Guidelines

The Patent Office has articulated a multi-step test for evaluating the eligibility of claims under 35 U.S.C. § 101. See IPEP 2106(III). Step 1 asks whether the claim is directed to a process, a machine, an article of manufacture, or a composition of matter. See id. If not, the claim is not eligible; if so, the claim is analyzed under Step 2A. See id. Step 2A, Prong 1 asks whether the claim recites a judicial exception (i.e., a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea). See id. at page 15. If not, the claim is patent eligible; if so, further analysis is required under Step 2A, Prong 2. See id. Step 2A, Prong 2 asks whether the claim recites additional elements that integrate the exception into a practical application of the exception. See id. at page 16. If so, the claim is eligible; if not, further analysis under step 2B is required. See id. Step 2B asks whether

the claim recites additional elements that amount to "significantly more" (e.g., an inventive concept) than the abstract idea. See id. at pages 22 and 23. If yes, the claim is eligible; if not, the claim is not eligible. See id.
Independent claim 18 is patent eligible.

Although the Applicant does not necessarily agree with the rejection of independent claim 18, the Applicant presently amends claim 18 to expedite prosecution. As amended, claim 18 recites, inter alia,

receiving, at one or more processors, first data indicative of a carbon dioxide (CO2) concentration in exhaled breath of a subject from a CO2 sensor of a CO2 sensing system and second data indicative of information associated with a tubing system in response to the tubing system being coupled to the CO2 sensing system, wherein the second data is received from a communication
component associated with the tubing system; and
changing, by the one or more processors, an operation mode of the CO2 sensing system during operation of the CO2 sensing system based on the second data indicative of the information
associated with the tubing system.

The Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claim 18 is patent eligible. Indeed, as mentioned in the Interview Summary above, the Examiner indicated that the amendments presented in amended claim 18 appear to overcome the current rejection. Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of claims 18-20, 25-29, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 101.

In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 18, 26, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly anticipated by Weiss et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2016/0073929; hereinafter "Weiss"). The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
Legal Precedent
Anticipation under section 102 can be found only if a single reference shows exactly what is claimed. Titanium Metals Corp. v. Banner, 778 F.2d 775, 227 U.S.P.Q. 773 (Fed. Cir. 1985).

For a prior art reference to anticipate under section 102, every element of the claimed invention must be identically shown in a single reference. In re Bond, 910 F.2d 831, 15 U.S.P.Q.2d 1566 (Fed. Cir. 1990). To maintain a proper rejection under section 102, a single reference must teach each and every limitation of the rejected claim. Atlas Powder v. E.I. du Pont, 750 F.2d 1569 (Fed. Cir. 1984). Accordingly, the Applicant needs only point to a single element not found in the cited reference to demonstrate that the cited reference fails to anticipate the claimed subject matter. The prior art reference also must show the identical invention "in as complete detail as contained in the... claim" to support a prima facie case of anticipation. Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236, 9 U.S.P.Q. 2d 1913, 1920 (Fed. Cir. 1989).
Weiss does not anticipate independent claim 18.

Although the Applicant does not necessarily agree with the rejection of independent claims 18, the Applicant presently amends claims 18 to expedite prosecution. As amended, claim 18 recites, inter alia,

receiving, at one or more processors, first data indicative of a carbon dioxide (CO2) concentration in exhaled breath of a subject from a CO2 sensor of a CO2 sensing system and second data indicative of information associated with a tubing system in response to the tubing system being coupled to the CO2 sensing system, wherein the second data is received from a communication
component associated with the tubing system; and
changing, by the one or more processors, an operation mode of the CO2 sensing system during operation of the CO2 sensing system based on the second data indicative of the information
associated with the tubing system.

The Applicant respectfully submits that Weiss is silent as to at least these features of amended claim 18, and thus cannot anticipate amended claim 18. Indeed, as mentioned in the Interview Summary above, the Examiner indicated that the amendments presented in amended

claim 18 appear to overcome the current rejection. Accordingly, the Applicant submits that Weiss does not disclose all elements of amended claim 18, and thus cannot anticipate amended claim 18. Additionally, the Applicant submits that Weiss does not disclose all elements of dependent claims 26 and 31, at least because of their dependency on independent claim 18, and thus cannot anticipate these dependent claims. Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of claims 18, 26, and 31 under 35 U.S.C. § 102.

In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 19 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over Weiss in view of Colman et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2014/0014729; hereinafter "Colman '729"); claim 25 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over Weiss in view of Coleman et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2017/0325716; hereinafter "Coleman '716"); claim 27 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over Weiss in view of Colman et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2009/0275851; hereinafter "Colman '851") and Boyer (U.S. Publication No. 2016/0093205; hereinafter "Boyer"); claim 28 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over Weiss in view of Colman et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2010/0317986; hereinafter "Colman '986"); claim 29 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over Weiss in view of Colman et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2011/0040713; hereinafter "Colman '713"); and claim 30 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over Weiss in view of Ben-Oren et al. (U.S. Patent No. 6,656,127; hereinafter "Ben-Oren"). The Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.
Legal Precedent

The burden of establishing a prima facie case of obviousness falls on the Examiner. Ex parte Wolters and Kuypers, 214 U.S.P.Q. 735 (B.P.A.I. 1979). To establish prima facie obviousness of a claimed invention, all the claim limitations must be taught or suggested by the prior art. In re Royka, 180 U.S.P.Q. 580 (C.C.P.A. 1974). However, a claimed invention composed of several elements is not proved obvious merely by demonstrating that each of its elements was, independently, known in the prior art. KSR International Co. v. Teleflex Inc., 127 S.Ct. 1727, 1741 (2007). The KSR court stated that "it can be important to identify a reason that would have prompted a person of ordinary skill in the relevant field to combine the elements in

the way the claimed new invention does ... because inventions in most, if not all, instances rely upon building blocks long since uncovered, and claimed discoveries almost of necessity will be combinations of what, in some sense, is already known." Id. Specifically, there must be some articulated reasoning with a rational underpinning to support a conclusion of obviousness; a conclusory statement will not suffice. In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977, 988 (Fed. Cir. 2006). Indeed, the factual inquiry determining whether to combine references must be thorough and searching, and it must be based on objective evidence of record. In re Lee, 61 U.S.P.Q.2d 1430, 1436 (Fed. Cir. 2002).
Dependent claims 19, 20, 25, and 27-30.

Claims 19, 20, 25, and 27-30 depend from amended independent claim 18. As mentioned above, claim 18 is allowable over Weiss. In addition, the Applicant respectfully submits that Colman '729, Coleman '716, Colman '851, Boyer, Colman '986, Colman '713, and Ben-Oren do not cure the deficiencies of Weiss with respect to claim 18, and thus cannot support aprimafacie case of obviousness for claims 19, 20, 25, and 27-30. Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of claims 19, 20, 25, and 27-30 under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

As noted above, the Applicant adds new claims 32-35, which recite additional features not disclosed by the cited references. Support for the new claims may be found in at least paragraphs 46-49, 56, and 57 of the originally filed specification. The Applicant notes that no excess claims fees are due for the new claims. The Applicant respectfully requests allowance of the new claims based at least on their respective dependencies from independent claim 18, as well as the separate elements therein.
